title: Northern Lights could be seen in UK - will they be visible in skies above Lancs?
excerpt: The Northern Lights will be visible in skies above parts of the UK on Wednesday - but will they be visible across Lancashire?
content:
Northern lights from Pendle Hill (Image: Steve Bradley Photography)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

The Northern Lights will be visible in skies above parts of the UK on Wednesday - but will they be visible across Lancashire?

It is bad news for stargazers in Lancashire as the Met Office has said that while there is a chance of increased auroral activity later this week due to changing space weather, the best views are expected further north in Scotland.

Natalia Wells, a spokesperson for the Met Office, said: "Space weather conditions are expected to become more active later this week as a faster stream of solar wind reaches Earth.

"Current forecasts suggest the best chance of any aurora sightings will be across parts of Scotland, where skies are clear.

"While it is not impossible that some slight auroral enhancement may be detectable further south through cameras, including in Lancashire, this is considered unlikely based on the current forecast."

She also cautioned that visibility will depend on several factors.

She said: "Any visibility will depend on the strength of the geomagnetic activity and local viewing conditions, with cloud cover and light of the nearly full moon affecting the chances of seeing the aurora during the first half of the night."

The Met Office explained that fast solar winds are expected to arrive later in the week, bringing a chance of auroras on Wednesday, September 23, and Thursday, September 24, particularly over parts of Scotland.

In East Lancashire, heavy rain and mostly cloudy conditions are forecast during the day on Wednesday, but skies are expected to clear from 5pm.
